correctness.rationale: For r>=2, m_i>=1, t=2^p and zero-sum vertex coefficients, eliminating the hub yields the exact distance-power quadratic Q=-sum_{i,a} x_{i,a}^2+(1-t)sum_i s_i^2+(t-2)(sum_i s_i)^2, with s_i the blade totals. The sharp inequality sum_a x_{i,a}^2>=s_i^2/m_i reduces conditional negativity to a diagonal form a_i=t-1+1/m_i and a rank-one correction. Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz gives the necessary and sufficient F(t)=(t-2)sum_i a_i^-1<=1 (for t>2), with equality vector and strict sign witness. F strictly increases from 0 at t=2 to r>1; hence a unique t_*>2. Strictness below and one-dimensional endpoint radical follow from equality conditions; basepoint Euclidean Gram rank is M below and M-1 at the endpoint. Concavity of g_t(m)=m/((t-1)m+1) and integral unit transfers classify unique balanced and extreme partitions for fixed r,M. Independently constructed small bouquet zero-sum matrices and found their maximal eigenvalue zero at the computed t_*; finite checks do not replace these all-size arguments.
residual_risks: The theorem covers one shared hub and unweighted shortest-path distances; not arbitrary connected block graphs or weighted graphs.
The unequal-size exponent is implicit in a unique monotone scalar root.
